Official Fort Bend County and Texas State Directory pages document Wong's covered county role and Republican affiliation. The matter remains a disputed political and administrative conflict: no final court ruling or official misconduct finding was located, and only one independent report was found. Quarantine retains the retaliation allegation and denial without converting it into an established misconduct event.

coverage_gaps: North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Kansas, Oklahoma, Texas, Colorado, New Mexico, and Arizona attorney-general, ethics, court, public-safety, corrections, licensing, election, and major local-government indexes were checked. No additional current-window person-specific event meeting the covered-role, timing, and explicit-affiliation rules was identified.

The current Texas Tribune/ProPublica report about Ken Paxton's voter-registration history was retained as a quarantine lead because it was not independently corroborated by a separate report and did not document a charge, complaint, or official finding; Paxton's campaign did not directly answer the reported finding.

The Houston Press report about Fort Bend County's legal-office reorganization was retained as a quarantine lead because the retaliation claim is disputed, the official adjudication remains pending, and only one independent report was located despite an on-record denial from Wong's communications director.

Colorado court dockets, Mesa County and Pueblo County blotter archives, and local law-enforcement logs exposed routine criminal matters and procedural listings without a qualifying political or affiliated-organizational role; they were not treated as evidence of absence.

The September 2 DOJ indictment of Tulsa resident Deleon Cooks was routed to A04 as a federal matter and did not qualify for an A09 event because no covered public role or qualifying affiliation was documented.

The September 1 report about former Fountain councilwoman Detra Duncan was a procedural ruling in a 2025 case, and the official Fountain page identifies council elections as nonpartisan. The Colorado candidate follow-up concerning Democrat Christian Schilder involved a May arrest and was excluded under the affiliation and timing rules.

Several state and county systems are dynamic, fragmented, date-limited, or not uniformly time-filtered; some national and local news pages were blocked or only partially retrievable through the web interface. These limitations are recorded as coverage gaps, not evidence of no misconduct.

Routine private-person arrests, federal matters owned by another lane, policy disputes, campaign accusations, and matters involving people without a qualifying public role or documented affiliation were excluded. Central merge/publication was not run for this individual scan.
